title: Nuevo Laredo property tax collection tops 200 million pesos for the first time
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo’s property tax collection surpassed 200 million pesos for the first time in the city’s history, up 18 percent from the same period last year, the municipal government announced — and the city says it has also paid off the entire 580 million pesos of inherited public debt.
content:
Nuevo Laredo’s property tax collection surpassed 200 million pesos for the first time in the city’s history, growing 18 percent compared with the same period last year, according to the municipal government.

About 90,000 of the city’s roughly 199,000 registered property accounts have paid the tax so far, according to municipal records cited in the report.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal credited residents’ trust in the city government, saying that when people see their contributions turned into public works, better services and infrastructure in their neighborhoods, they respond by participating.

The city also reported it has fully paid off 580 million pesos of inherited public debt, leaving Nuevo Laredo with no public debt and more capacity to direct resources toward city development, according to the report.

Tax incentives offered during 2026 have saved families more than 70 million pesos in surcharges, fees and enforcement costs tied to the property tax, according to the city.

Through November, the city is waiving 100 percent of surcharges, fees and collection costs on overdue property tax, and 100 percent of surcharges on the real estate acquisition tax, to help residents regularize their accounts and secure legal certainty over their property.

A parking-meter regularization program is also in effect, offering a 50 percent discount on fines and a 100 percent waiver of surcharges on violations accumulated since 2022. The city reports about 65,000 pending fines worth around 18 million pesos.

Residents can make payments at municipal cashier modules, and parking-meter fines can also be paid at OXXO stores. For guidance, residents can visit the Revenue offices on the ground floor of the El Palomar building, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

Sources: El Reportero de Tamaulipas, November 10, 2026; El Gráfico Tamaulipas, November 10, 2026.
